column2: Step
Agree the time with the department and collect the users' list of complaints
Record serial number, software version, probe list and on-screen errors; export logs before changing anything
Quick image check on every probe before maintenance
Proper software shutdown, then mains disconnection before cleaning
Clean or replace every air filter; confirm every fan runs quietly; record temperatures if available
Inspect and clean probe ports; test recognition of every probe in every working port
Check the cart: wheels, brakes, lifting column, monitor arm, cable hooks, probe holders, mains cord
Clean the control panel with approved agents; clean and test trackball, keys, encoders, TGC sliders, touch screen
Check monitor, printers and other peripherals the department uses
Check UPS status and age, internal batteries for swelling and run time, date and time
Check free disk space; back up presets and configuration to hospital-controlled media and record where
Send a test image to PACS and query the worklist
No software updates, options or licence changes without authorisation
Electrical safety (lesson 5), image quality (lesson 7), report (lesson 8)
Confirm the probe has been reprocessed; wear gloves; record model and serial number first
Ask what was seen, in which preset, since when, after what event, and on which ports
Inspect in a fixed order: lens, housing, strain reliefs, cable, connector, system port; photograph findings
Run the air image test, flex the cable at both ends, and repeat on a second port
Locate gaps with a moist finger or a smooth wire; remember phased arrays may hide dead elements
Compare with the phantom baseline for that probe, and use a probe tester where available
Record one decision — in service, watch, repair or withdraw — tag the probe and inform the department in writing
